_meta.indication: Prophylaxis to prevent attacks of hereditary angioedema (HAE) in patients 12 years and older

pivotal_trials.design: 26-week, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial; subjects randomized 2:1 to lanadelumab or placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Patients ≥ 12 years of age with Type I or II hereditary angioedema
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: number of investigator-confirmed HAE attacks during the treatment period (Days 0-182)
pivotal_trials.n: 126 randomized, 125 treated (Placebo N=41; lanadelumab 150 mg Q4W N=28, 300 mg Q4W N=29, 300 mg Q2W N=27)
pivotal_trials.result: LS mean monthly HAE attack rate 0.26 (95% CI 0.14, 0.46) for lanadelumab 300 mg Q2W vs 1.97 (1.64, 2.36) for placebo; adjusted p<0.001 for all three doses (150 mg Q4W 0.48; 300 mg Q4W 0.53)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions: injection site reactions (52% total vs 34% placebo), upper respiratory infection (29% vs 32%), headache (21% vs 22%); hypersensitivity reactions observed (1% vs 0%); asymptomatic, transient transaminase (AST/ALT) elevations
target_moa: Fully human monoclonal antibody (IgG1κ) that inhibits active plasma kallikrein, reducing bradykinin generation and thereby preventing HAE attacks

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the application did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues requiring outside expertise

description.text: Expanded use to pediatric patients 2 to <12 years for prophylaxis to prevent HAE attacks

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics license application provides for the expanded use of Takhzyro in pediatric patients 2 to < 12 years of age for prophylaxis to prevent attacks of hereditary angioedema (HAE).
